newsitem.title: USA: USAir says Eastern US leaders back Heathrow bid.
newsitem.headline: USAir says Eastern US leaders back Heathrow bid.

text.p: Politicians and businesses in the eastern U.S. urged the U.S. Transportation Department to reach an "open skies" air accord with Britain and to award new London routes to USAir Group Inc, USAir said Wednesday.
It said the letters were from more than 70 U.S. senators and representatives and several dozen from governors, mayors, state legislators, city leaders and businesses.

USAir said the letters stressed the importance to the economy of an "open skies" agreement and of ensuring USAir as a competitor in the U.S.-British market before any approval of the proposed alliance of American Airlines, a unit of AMR Corp, and British Airways Plc.
USAir has asked for approval for new routes to London's Heathrow airport from Boston; Charlotte, N.C.; Philadelphia; and Pittsburgh.
The United States and Britain have been trying to agree on ending restrictions on aviation services between their countries, but little or no progress has been made.
U.S. officials have said an "open skies" pact had to be reached with Britain before it could approve the American Air/British Air alliance.
